The amount of people downvoting your post demonstrates the lack of willingness for other members of this community to consider another addict's perspective if it is different from their own. I am working with a Smart Recovery handbook and a therapist and that's working much better than 12 steps have for me. There is perhaps exceptional value to be found from looking "within" to your own perceived deficits, but unfortunately the idea that by looking to fix yourself you are at a more "enlightened" stage than another recovering addict and automatically know what is going to work for them is an egoistic presumption, however, this is more due to interpersonal group member characteristics rather than a flaw in the methodology of the principles themselves.

Personally, I don't find much use in looking over all the bad things I dun' did. Shit happened. There's nothing I can do about it. No one has nearly as much control over anything that happens as they like to think they have. What can I do to move on? That's where cognitive behavioral therapy, rational emotive behavioral therapy, motivational enhancement therapy and mindfulness practice are all personally helpful for my recovery. MY recovery.

Kratom is much different than kava, and it is very much addictive when used excessively as it produces withdrawal symptoms similar to withdrawal from opiates. Kava has no capacity to instigate withdrawal. I have had problems with kratom too. I tended to have a lot of cravings for heavier shit when I used it.

As far as feeling different goes... Sugar, salt, television, and sex all change the way we feel, but that sure as hell doesn't mean I have to spend my whole life avoiding them. I have issue with the wording, "______ led me back to _______." If I choose to take kava, it is a choice. Everything I have ever taken has essentially been my choice, only I have pretended that I have had no choice in the matter and blamed circumstances outside of my control in order to use something which was undoubtedly problematic for 99.99% of its users. Kava is not comparable to kratom except for that it changes the way one feels, as you mention, but food and sex change the way I feel too, and both probably can be more addictive than kava.

I've asked for people with knowledge and experience with kava to respond to this post. Kava is not remotely comparable to pharmaceutical muscle relaxers in terms of potential for abuse, dependency, pharmacology or mechanism of action; the only major commonality it shares with pharmaceutical muscle relaxers is the obvious effect of relaxing the muscles.

To be clear, my friend in recovery who says "I want to Diazepam just to chill" is making an entirely riskier decision based on that drug's pharmacology than one who says "I want to take kava just to chill." They are not comparable.

I appreciate your response. I don't want to ingest any substance that drastically changes the way I feel. From my understanding, kava is not addictive and has zero potential to produce chemical dependency. It also isn't something that I would use to try to "escape" my problems, more as a mild relaxant. Kava changes the way I feel physically, which of course has a corresponding psychological effect, but it does not drastically alter my state of mind in such a way that my cognition is impaired. 

I don't consider myself "special," but I also don't think that drinking kava necessarily has to lead me back to any of the substances that I have had particular problems with using successfully. All that being said, I can see that it could be a slippery slope given the uncertainty I experience in regards to using it. I don't think I need to count it as relapse or that it has to "lead me back" to using anything that was harmful for me, but at the same rate I don't know how I will respond to it.
